y_voice_2.text: I don't want to be blocked from using social media just because of my age. If even high school students couldn't have accounts, I think it would be hard to keep in touch with friends. I'm against a ban. I want to have a say in what I can use and how I use it. I want to decide for myself, but I can't handle everything that happens on my own. If people say bad things about me or threaten me, I'd still want to turn to an adult right away. Maybe that's selfish of me. Rather than putting the same limits on how everyone can use it based on age, I think there are other things we can do, like setting safety filters. I want the approach to change so it takes our use into account, without even stopping us from keeping in touch with friends.

y_voice_3.text: As a parent raising a middle school child, I want to decide how much to let them use social media based on what they can handle. Rather than drawing the line by age alone, I think it would be better, if possible, for the features they can use to grow step by step as they become able to handle more. I don't want the choice to be only between letting them use it and banning it. I want to set different stages. If my child started using social media with no preparation the moment they passed the age when it had been banned, that would worry me. I don't think reaching the age when it's okay to use it means they'll suddenly know how to protect themselves. Just as you need to practice swimming before going into the sea, it's still scary when a child who isn't ready is suddenly thrown into it.

The question of setting an age when children are allowed to use social media also raises the question of how much they can turn to adults after they start.
